\caption{Bin-characterisation points for all 490 published bins of the high-$Q^{2}$ charged-hadron SIDIS measurement (245 per charge; cone+S2$'$ observable basis, Born-level cross sections with $Z$-boson exchange included in the correction convention, coherent body+miss RAPGAP31 prior; $\mathcal{L} = 351~\mathrm{pb}^{-1}$). Each row gives the Born-level cross section $\sigma_{\mathrm{B}}$ integrated over the bin (nb, not a density) with its total uncertainty $\delta^{\mathrm{tot}}$ (the published 15-component leg-envelope total relative uncertainty, including its statistical component, converted to absolute on $\sigma_{\mathrm{B}}$), followed by the cross-section-weighted marginal means $\langle v\rangle$ of seven kinematic variables, each with its statistical uncertainty $\sigma^{\mathrm{stat}}$ and model uncertainty $\sigma^{\mathrm{mod}}$ (column triple order: value, $\sigma^{\mathrm{stat}}$, $\sigma^{\mathrm{mod}}$). The means are RAD-level-iteration values obtained with an iterative data--MC tilt correction: the RAPGAP31 cone+S2$'$ gen-level population is reweighted until its tilted spectrum matches the IBU $k=4$ unfolded data spectrum. $\sigma^{\mathrm{stat}}$ is the 200-toy propagation of the IBU covariance through the tilt iteration; $\sigma^{\mathrm{mod}}$ is the $|\mathrm{RAPGAP31}-\mathrm{DJANGOH14}|$ generator difference. The Born-vs-RAW level sensitivity of each position is carried separately (signed \texttt{level\_borndelta}, machine-readable companion only; reaching up to about $\pm 10\%$ of $\langle Q^{2}\rangle$ in the S3 stratum, per-bin extremes $-13.8\%$/$+12.0\%$). The seven marginal means characterise the bin but do NOT form a consistent four-dimensional kinematic point: the $y$ derived from $(\langle Q^{2}\rangle, \langle x\rangle)$ differs from the quoted $\langle y\rangle$ (excess of the quoted over the derived value) by $+8$ to $+10\%$ typically in the narrow S0--S2 cells (per-stratum medians; individual bins up to $+22.4\%$), by up to $+63\%$ in populated S3 bins and by up to $+96\%$ in the worst affected sparse S3 corner (16 data entries), with the $W$ derived from the same pair shifted by up to $+42\%$ (broad-bin Jensen effects). Theory predictions must therefore be compared bin-integrated over the published bin volumes (as defined for the appendix cross-section tables, with the $x$ width capped at $1-x_{\min}$ in the S3$_{x0}$ cell), with the values of this table serving as the bin characterisation only. The three position-uncertainty components ($\sigma^{\mathrm{stat}}$, $\sigma^{\mathrm{mod}}$, level) are quoted separately; no combined position uncertainty is defined (the combination policy is an open decision). $\sigma^{\mathrm{stat}}(x)$ is exactly zero in the S3 cell (single-bin $x$ families receive no tilt, so no data-statistical information reaches the $x$ position). The bins with zero reconstructed-data entries ((h$^{+}$,109), (h$^{+}$,179), (h$^{-}$,240)) retain MC-population-based positions. Units: $Q^{2}$ in GeV$^{2}$; $p_{T,h}$ and $W$ in GeV; $x$, $y$, $z$ and $\varepsilon$ dimensionless; cross sections in nb. The values are preliminary and subject to change.}
\label{tab:app:bincenter-points}\\
